question: Assume today is 2026-10-19. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the turnover of Taiwan's food and beverage services industry (餐飲業營業額, current prices) in September 2026, in New Taiwan dollars (TWD), as it will be first reported in the Ministry of Economic Affairs Department of Statistics' monthly release on wholesale, retail and food services turnover (批發、零售及餐飲業營業額統計).

target.what: Monthly turnover (revenue, current prices) of Taiwan's food and beverage services industry (餐飲業營業額), as reported in the MOEA Department of Statistics monthly release on wholesale, retail and food services turnover; total industry, domestic activity, all enterprise sizes covered by the survey
target.publisher: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Statistics (經濟部統計處)
target.cadence: monthly, first reported roughly 20-25 days after month end
target.caveats: Target period is completed relative to cutoff 2026-10-19 but the September 2026 figure is not yet published at cutoff; the first release is the target. Definition is nominal (current-price) turnover of food and beverage service enterprises, not retail food sales, not wholesale, not GDP restaurant va

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 turnover = September 2025 turnover grown by the recent year-on-year growth rate, adjusted for calendar (Mid-Autumn Festival timing, number of weekend days) and price effects; the target's own recent monthly series and prior-year September value anchor the level.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly 餐飲業營業額 for Jan 2024 through Aug 2026 (published before cutoff), especially September 2025 value and YoY growth rates for 2025-2026 months; also the August 2026 release figure and any July/August 2026 YoY growth.

assumptions.name: Chain-to-industry growth transfer factor (chain YoY growth relative to industry YoY growth)
assumptions.rationale: Listed chains grew far faster than the industry in September 2026 (Wowprime +19.85% Taiwan, Hi-Lai +25.77%, Kanpai +20.97%, Bafang +8.36%, TTFB +8.86%, Young Qin +17.26%, but Jhujian -16.23%), while the industry grew only ~1.8% in August and is forecast +3-6% in September; chains are expanding store counts and gaining share, so their growth overstates industry growth by roughly a factor of two.
assumptions.applies_when: The listed-chain aggregate is used as a growth proxy and must be damped to the industry's broader, slower-growing base.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that chain and industry growth moved one-for-one in prior Septembers, or a September 2026 industry print near the chain aggregate.

methods.label: m1

p137.role: September 2025 total food-service turnover level (base month)

a1.role: September 2026 YoY growth factor relative to September 2025

methods.rationale: Own-history route: September 2025 level times a YoY growth factor anchored on MOEA's own September 2026 forecast (+3-6%). Shared dependency: the base level and the forecast both come from MOEA; failure mode is that the forecast misses the holiday effect.

methods.label: m2

a3.role: September 2026 real volume growth of food service (fraction)

methods.rationale: Deflator decomposition: nominal growth = menu-price inflation (外食費, above 3% per p71/p72) plus real volume growth. Independent of the MOEA forecast; failure mode is that real volume is unobserved and menu inflation is only bounded below.
methods.error: input a3: assumption a3 was rejected (need 0 < low <= value <= high)

methods.label: m4

p207.role: Wowprime Taiwan business group September 2026 YoY growth, as the chain-level growth signal

a4.role: chain-to-industry growth transfer factor damping the chain signal to industry growth

methods.rationale: Improved chain route: uses Wowprime's Taiwan-only growth (+19.85%, p207) damped by a transfer factor because listed chains are gaining share and growing faster than the industry. Failure mode is that the transfer factor is uncertain and Wowprime may not represent the chain aggregate.

methods.label: m5

a4.role: chain-to-industry growth transfer factor damping the chain signal to industry growth

methods.rationale: Broader chain aggregate: mean growth of several listed chains (Bafang, TTFB, Young Qin) damped by the transfer factor. Cross-checks m4; failure mode is that the chain set is small and excludes the strongest and weakest performers.

excluded_by_input_audit.label: m3
excluded_by_input_audit.reason: input audit: p124: Wowprime is a single restaurant chain; its YoY growth is not the industry-wide growth, and no conversion input bridges chain-level to industry-level growth.

kept.name: September 2026 YoY growth factor for food-service turnover
kept.rationale: Anchored on MOEA's own September 2026 forecast of +3% to +6% (p111), midpoint 4.5%; the 4-day Mid-Autumn/Teachers' Day holiday (p177-p179) and food-away-from-home inflation above 3% (p71, p72) support the midpoint rather than the low end, while August's weak +1.8% (p233) and the soft restaurant sub-
kept.applies_when: The MOEA forecast is a genuine nowcast of the same total-industry, current-price series and the September calendar effect is as described.
kept.falsified_by: A September 2026 print outside 854-879億元, or evidence that the holiday boost was much weaker than in prior Mid-Autumn-in-September years.

kept.name: September 2026 food-away-from-home price growth
kept.rationale: Food-away-from-home inflation has exceeded 3% for four consecutive months as of September 2026 (p71, p72); general CPI is +2.73% (p68), so menu prices sit modestly above headline CPI.
kept.applies_when: Menu-price inflation in September 2026 is close to the recent 3%+ run rate.
kept.falsified_by: A reported 外食費 YoY below 2.5% or above 4% for September 2026.

kept.name: Chain-to-industry growth transfer factor (chain YoY growth relative to industry YoY growth)
kept.rationale: Listed chains grew far faster than the industry in September 2026 (Wowprime +19.85% Taiwan, Hi-Lai +25.77%, Kanpai +20.97%, Bafang +8.36%, TTFB +8.86%, Young Qin +17.26%, but Jhujian -16.23%), while the industry grew only ~1.8% in August and is forecast +3-6% in September; chains are expanding store
kept.applies_when: The listed-chain aggregate is used as a growth proxy and must be damped to the industry's broader, slower-growing base.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that chain and industry growth moved one-for-one in prior Septembers, or a September 2026 industry print near the chain aggregate.

rejected.name: September 2026 real volume growth of food service
rejected.rationale: Nominal growth of ~4.5% minus ~3.2% price inflation leaves ~1.3% real; consistent with the modest real momentum implied by August's +1.8% nominal against 3%+ menu inflation.
rejected.applies_when: Real dining volume grows modestly, aided by the 4-day holiday but held back by soft restaurant traffic.
rejected.falsified_by: Evidence of a sharp real-volume surge or contraction in September 2026 dining.

residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
